brief_data.deck: Glow, the Tel Aviv and Palo Alto endpoint-security company founded in 2025 by former Meta engineering VP Roi Tiger, emerged from stealth on 22 July 2026 with $180M raised at a $1.2B valuation, led by Sequoia, Cyberstarts, Greenoaks and Redpoint, with paying customers and a US go-to-market team to build.

risks.label: EARLY-STAGE CAPACITY
risks.detail: Glow is a year old with about 100 staff and no disclosed revenue; the $180M funds research and sales before brand.
risks.counter: Price at the Haas partner tier with product as part-payment; make the deployment the first proof point.

risks.label: CROWDED CATEGORY
risks.detail: Six security vendors already hold F1 seats; a seventh, unknown logo can be invisible.
risks.counter: Lead with the prevention-first, AI-agent story the incumbents do not tell, and the Wiz-alumni leadership.

extended.ask: A 25-minute call with Roi Tiger before the United States GP to confirm the round structure on the record, walk through a Haas device deployment, and size an Official Endpoint Security Partner entry, part-paid in product, against the team's 2027 roster.

value.text: A Formula 1 engineering staff runs the tools Glow polices: developer environments, package managers, AI coding agents and copilots on laptops that join a different circuit network 24 weekends a year. Glow's living asset inventory maps what runs on every device, its policy engine blocks risky packages and unsanctioned agents before they execute, and it flags devices where detection tools have gone quiet, the gaps the release says it has already found at customers.
value.label: Operational workstream (Mode A)

value.text: Prevention that stops software and agents at the door reduces the alert load on a small IT team, which matters to a privateer spending inside the FIA cost cap. Product can form part of the consideration, lowering the cash element of the deal.
value.label: Cost-cap arithmetic

value.text: Glow sells to CISOs and security leaders at enterprises in healthcare, retail and financial services, an audience Haas's current partners do not bring to the suite. US-race hospitality for those prospects and a factory reference story give the team a new guest list and Glow its first named reference deployment.
value.label: Commercial lift for the team

value.text: Official Endpoint Security Partner designation, sidepod or halo placement, a published deployment case study with the team's IT leadership, hospitality at Miami, Austin and Las Vegas, and driver and engineering access for Glow's customer events and Glow Labs content.
value.label: What the team gives back

why_now.text: On 22 July 2026 Glow emerged from stealth with $180M in funding at a $1.2B valuation. The company's release names the leads, Sequoia, Cyberstarts, Greenoaks and Redpoint Ventures, and the participants, Index Ventures, Swish Ventures, Lux Capital, Operator Collective and Holly Ventures, and states the use of funds: accelerating the go-to-market team in the United States and expanding Glow Labs, its research arm.
why_now.label: Trigger

why_now.text: CTech reports the $180M as a $20M seed led by Sequoia and Cyberstarts, a $60M Series A led by Index Ventures with Greenoaks at a $400M valuation, and a $100M Series B, all in roughly a year; the company itself gives only the total, so the split is reported, not confirmed. Whatever the split, a company that tripled its valuation inside a year before showing a product has investors expecting a category to be built, and category-building is brand spend.
why_now.label: Three rounds in a year

why_now.text: The stated use of funds is a US go-to-market team. A security vendor's first brand line typically opens with its first enterprise sales cycle, and CISO-facing hospitality is what the other six security vendors on the grid bought. Glow is at the front of that cycle, not the end of it.
why_now.label: The first brand budget follows the first sales hires

why_now.text: The United States GP in Austin (October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the US rounds left in 2026, and teams close their 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. A deal agreed before Austin can be announced in Glow's chosen sales market and activated in full for 2027.
why_now.label: Calendar window

why_team.text: Haas carries Toyota Gazoo Racing as title and technical partner, Mphasis as Official Digital Partner, CommScope and Ruckus for connectivity and Orion180 for insurance, and no security vendor. The team profile lists cybersecurity (product) as an open category; Mphasis sells cyber services, so it is a channel for a deployment rather than a clash.
why_team.label: An explicitly open lane

why_team.text: Haas is the grid's lean American privateer. Its partner tier is one a year-old company with $180M can carry without distorting its budget, and product can form part of the consideration. The bigger teams' security lanes are taken; the open ones at Cadillac and Racing Bulls come without the explicit open-category listing Haas has.
why_team.label: Priced for a 100-person company

why_team.text: Glow's raise funds a US go-to-market team from a Palo Alto base. Haas is headquartered in Kannapolis, North Carolina, with three home races a year at Miami, Austin and Las Vegas, where the CISOs Glow is hiring to reach already gather.
why_team.label: American team, American sales market

why_team.text: CrowdStrike at Mercedes, Bitdefender at Ferrari, Keeper at Williams, 1Password (Red Bull), Cato Networks at Alpine and NinjaOne at Audi each hold a security or endpoint lane; McLaren carries Cisco and Okta; Aston Martin has a SentinelOne history. Of the open teams, Haas combines the open-category listing, the US identity and a price that fits.
why_team.label: Ruled out by the table

ruled_out.reason: CrowdStrike holds the cybersecurity lane; endpoint protection is a direct clash.
Bitdefender is the cybersecurity partner and an endpoint rival.
Keeper occupies identity and privileged-access security.
Cato Networks joined in 2026 and covers security.
NinjaOne (endpoint management) joined the roster; the endpoint lane is crowded.
Cisco covers security and networking and Okta covers identity.
SentinelOne, Official Cybersecurity Partner since 2021 with an extension announced in February 2024, is a direct endpoint rival; the table lists it as departed, so the lane is contested at best.

ruled_out.team: Cadillac F1 Team · Visa Cash App Racing Bulls
ruled_out.reason: Open but not chosen: neither lists cybersecurity as an open category the way Haas does, and Cadillac's partner tier is priced above a year-old company.

brief_data.bottom_line: A $180M stealth exit at $1.2B, a Sequoia and Cyberstarts syndicate, paying customers and a funded US sales build put Glow at the start of its brand-spend cycle. Haas lists cybersecurity as an open category, the grid has proved security vendors buy F1 to reach CISOs, and two US races remain inside the window.

brief_data.the_case_p1: Glow's release states $180M in funding at a $1.2B valuation, led by Sequoia, Cyberstarts, Greenoaks and Redpoint Ventures, with Index, Swish, Lux, Operator Collective and Holly Ventures participating; CTech reports it as three rounds in about a year, a $20M seed, a $60M Series A at $400M and a $100M Series B. The product is prevention-first: it decides which software, AI agents and developer tools may run on employee devices rather than detecting them afterwards. Paying customers span healthcare, retail and financial services; the money goes to a US go-to-market team and Glow Labs.
brief_data.the_case_p2: Cybersecurity is the grid's most-sold technology category, and every vendor bought the same thing: CrowdStrike at Mercedes, Bitdefender at Ferrari, Keeper at Williams, Cato Networks at Alpine, a paddock full of the CISOs they sell to. Glow's leadership has run that playbook from inside: COO Emily Heath sat on Wiz's board through its $32B sale to Google and was a Cyberstarts partner. A stealth exit with $180M is when a company buys its stage.

brief_data.value_content: MODE A - operational. A race team's engineers run exactly the tools Glow polices: developer environments, package managers, AI agents and copilots on laptops that travel to 24 circuits. Glow maps what runs on every device, blocks risky packages and unsanctioned agents before they execute, and flags devices whose detection tools have gone quiet. Deployment across Kannapolis, Banbury and the trackside estate, a published case study, Glow Labs research on the team's threat surface.
brief_data.why_team_para: Haas lists cybersecurity as an open product category: Toyota Gazoo Racing as title and technical partner, Mphasis for digital services, CommScope and Ruckus for connectivity, and no security vendor. Mphasis sells cyber services, a channel for a deployment rather than a clash. The lean American privateer prices an entry a 100-person company can carry, Kannapolis sits in Glow's chosen sales market, and three US races a year put Glow in front of the CISOs it is hiring to reach.
brief_data.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Endpoint Security Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, 2027-2029, covering the US go-to-market build and the next raise. Estimated $2-4M a year, part-payable in product. Scope: sidepod or halo placement, deployment across the team's devices, US-race hospitality for CISO prospects, Glow Labs content.
brief_data.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  The stealth exit was 22 July and the stated use of funds is a US go-to-market team; the first brand budget follows the first sales hires. The United States GP in October and the Las Vegas GP in November sit inside the window, and teams close 2027 rosters in the fourth quarter.
brief_data.decision_maker_bio: Tiger founded Onavo, acquired by Meta, then spent nine years there, latterly as VP of Engineering; he fronts the launch and the raise. Path: Emily Heath, COO (former CISO of United Airlines and DocuSign, Wiz board); Arnon Joseph, Chief Product Officer. No chief marketing officer is listed.
brief_data.opening_angle_quote: “Roi, six security vendors already buy F1 to reach CISOs, and the American team has no security partner. You have just left stealth with $180M and a US sales team to build; a Haas deployment is reference customer and stage in one. 25 minutes before Austin?”
